clue.text: Perhaps killing time with Frank, add flavouring

blocks.note: frank and open both mean candid
to season food is to add flavouring

explanation.surface: Someone passing the time with a man called Frank while spicing up the cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a name at the start of a sentence; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Open season is the period when hunting a given animal is legal, so it is an example of a killing time.

clue.text: Working spell without delay

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A stint of work done promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' suggests magic, but it is a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving on time means punctually, with no lateness.

clue.text: Improve cover of Elton by Little Richard

indicators.note: a cover wraps around the outside, so only the outer letters are kept
little means shortened, so the name is cut down

blocks.note: first and last letters of Elton
the start of Richard

explanation.surface: Elton John making a better version of a Little Richard song.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard was the rock-and-roll star; here 'Little' shortens his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to improve its quality by adding to it.

clue.text: Game in southern resort: change from before?

blocks.note: S for south
Hove is a seaside resort next to Brighton
a coin from before decimal currency

explanation.surface: A pub game played at a south-coast resort, where the money may be out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: Shove-halfpenny is a British pub game sliding coins up a board; the halfpenny was an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shove-halfpenny is a traditional table game, so the answer is an example of a game.

clue.text: American with miserable cold?

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for American
pathetic means pitiful or wretched

explanation.surface: An American suffering with a nasty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like an illness; the question mark flags its sense of unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: An apathetic person shows no interest or emotion, which is one sense of being cold.

clue.text: Aleppo man in houses of certain Arabs

indicators.note: a phrase that houses something shelters it within its run of letters

blocks.note: letters running across the end of Aleppo, man and in

explanation.surface: A man from Aleppo living in the homes of some Arab people.
explanation.walkthrough: Aleppo is a Syrian city, steering thought away from the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Omani is the adjective for things belonging to Oman, an Arab country, so it describes certain Arabs.

clue.text: Surrounded by papers backing PM? Au contraire

indicators.note: French for 'on the contrary', telling the solver to swap the abbreviation for its opposite
backing here means standing behind and supporting, so the papers come after

blocks.note: the opposite of post meridiem is ante meridiem, morning
identity papers, ID

explanation.surface: A news item about the newspapers supporting the Prime Minister, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister but is the afternoon abbreviation; its contrary is the morning one.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of, which is the same as being surrounded by something.

clue.text: Land in gaol drunk after not very long?

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lurch into another order
after places the shuffled part behind the other piece

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, not very long at all
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone landing in prison for drunkenness after a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very long' seems to describe a sentence; it means a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongolia is a country in east Asia, and land is used for a country.

clue.text: Artiste could be Sudanese

indicators.note: could be suggests one thing turned into another, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer who might come from Sudan.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, a stage artiste.

clue.text: Make out sylvan region

blocks.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
sylvan means belonging to the woods

explanation.surface: A couple kissing in a forest glade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' looks like discern; it is slang for kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck of the woods is an idiom for a particular area or locality where someone lives.

clue.text: Trunk and tangled roots

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of their neat order, so the letters get mixed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk and its gnarled roots.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree picture hides that the trunk is a human one.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of a body is the torso, the part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Mycenaean king soon to host contest, leader of men

indicators.note: the leader of a group is the one in front, so take the opening letter
a host takes guests inside, so one word holds the others

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
a game is a contest
first letter of men

explanation.surface: A Greek king about to stage a competition for his soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soon' uses the archaic sense found in Shakespeare; the contest and the letter go in after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was the legendary king of Mycenae who led the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: Mum caught by Hebrew character in drama

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.surface: A mother caught out by a Hebrew-speaking figure in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' also hints at the play's superstition: actors keep mum about its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy, a classic stage drama.

clue.text: Annoying smoker reformed on island

indicators.note: reformed means made over into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiresome smoker who has kicked the habit while living on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the rearranged smoker after the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome is a synonym for annoying: something that irks causes irritation.

clue.text: One among two left dizzy in mad intellectual duel

indicators.note: among puts one item in the midst of others, so it goes inside
something dizzy is spinning and disordered, so its letters reel into a new order
in places the shuffled group inside the outer word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written
bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone stuck between two others feels giddy during a crazy cerebral contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'two' read as part of a scene, yet they are raw letters for the mix; the mixed group goes in before the last letter of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle of wits is a contest of cleverness, a duel fought with the mind rather than weapons.

clue.text: Russian fighter in East, respected, left country

indicators.note: in tells the solver where the fighter is placed, next to the compass point

blocks.note: E for east
the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
a rated performer is highly regarded

explanation.surface: A Russian soldier stationed in the East, well respected, defected abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a soldier, but it is an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to settle in another.

clue.text: Under pressure, puddings rising

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: puddings are desserts

explanation.surface: Puddings in the oven are rising under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed describes someone feeling strain or tension, as one does under pressure.

clue.text: Having finished pack, I smoked joint

blocks.note: something past is over and done
to ram is to pack tightly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who finished a pack of cigarettes, then smoked a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The smoking scene points to cigarettes and cannabis; the joint is meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked beef, cut from a joint of meat.

clue.text: Trade hardly busy? It could have us seeing red!

definitions.text: It could have us seeing red!

blocks.note: traffic means trade, as in trafficking goods
light traffic or light duties mean not busy

explanation.surface: A slow day in business, enough to make anyone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing red' looks like getting angry; here it is literally looking at a red signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic light shows red to stop drivers, so it is the thing that makes road users see red.

clue.text: At first Michael Caine transformed motion pictures

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the next word
transformed means changed in form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: first letter of Michael
taken as written

explanation.surface: Michael Caine changed the movies early in his career.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema is the art and industry of films, which are motion pictures.

clue.text: Adherent's initial sin admitted

indicators.note: initial means the opening letter of the word it qualifies

blocks.note: first letter of adherent
greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A follower confesses to wrongdoing at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed and admitted both mean conceded or accepted as true.

clue.text: Intense old lover leaves home, maiden installed

indicators.note: installed means fitted inside something, so one letter is put within

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a tree is where leaves live
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A passionate former partner moves out and a young woman moves in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves home' reads as someone departing; it is a description of a tree, home to leaves. A maiden is an over with no runs in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and intense both describe something of very great degree or force.

clue.text: Composer left in temper when sent up

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the other word
sent up in a down answer means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: rage is a fit of temper
L for left

explanation.surface: A composer left fuming after being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like mocked, but it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Writer having fish on line

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is written after it

blocks.note: a row is a line
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An author out angling, with a fish on the hook.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishing line is a row of things.
explanation.definitionFit: J. K. Rowling is the author of the Harry Potter novels, so she is a famous writer.

clue.text: Riotous celebration? Haggis laced with TNT!

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters run amok

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy party where the Scottish pudding has been spiked with explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggis is a Scottish dish of offal in a sheep's stomach. 'Riotous' looks like part of the definition but works on the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag night is a groom's party with his friends before the wedding, often a wild celebration.

clue.text: Abnormally fat alumnus feasted regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: an old boy of a school, OB
second, fourth and sixth letters of feasted

explanation.surface: A former pupil has put on weight from too much feasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese is the medical term for being overweight to a degree that harms health.

clue.text: Pathetic sort died: requiescat in pace

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for died
the Latin initials found on gravestones, rest in peace

explanation.surface: An obituary for a feeble person, complete with gravestone Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is informal for a weak, dull or ineffectual person.

clue.text: She who holds up the train?

definitions.text: She who holds up the train?

blocks.clueFragment: She who holds up the train?
blocks.note: surface reading: a woman delaying a railway train, perhaps a robber
setter's reading: a woman carrying the long trailing back of a wedding dress

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds up' suggests delaying or robbing, and 'train' a locomotive; the train is part of a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride at her wedding and often carries the dress's train behind her.
